answers.stem_only: Block SQL injection at layer 7 with no self-written rules: associate an AWS WAF web ACL with AWS managed rule groups (SQL database / core rule set) with the Application Load Balancer.

Per-IP flood from changing addresses while real users send few requests: an AWS WAF rate-based rule on a web ACL associated with the CloudFront distribution, which blocks each IP above a limit automatically and needs no IP list maintenance.

Low-and-slow credential stuffing from many IPs defeats per-IP rate limits; use the AWS WAF Fraud Control account takeover prevention (ATP) managed rule group on the login endpoint, which checks submitted credentials against stolen-credential data and failed-login patterns.
Layer 3/4 attacks such as SYN floods and UDP reflection, with no new subscription or configuration: AWS Shield Standard, which is automatic and free for CloudFront.

24/7 access to the Shield Response Team (needs Business or Enterprise Support) and cost protection credits: subscribe to AWS Shield Advanced now and add CloudFront and the ALB as protected resources before an attack, with an AWS WAF web ACL that has a rate-based rule (needed for layer 7 cost protection eligibility).

Central AWS WAF rules across an organization including new accounts: AWS Firewall Manager with an administrator account (prerequisites Organizations all features and AWS Config), one global WAF policy for CloudFront and one regional policy per Region for the ALBs, with auto remediation.

Web ACLs for CloudFront are global (CLOUDFRONT scope) and are created in US East (N. Virginia); recreate the web ACL and IP set there (IP sets are scoped the same way) and associate it with the distribution.

Create a dedicated firewall subnet with one Network Firewall endpoint in each Availability Zone, and route each zone's traffic symmetrically (both directions) through its same-zone endpoint, so one zone failure does not stop inspection elsewhere.

Layer 7 GET flood from many IPs, many known bots, cost-sensitive: AWS WAF web ACL on CloudFront with a rate-based rule plus the Amazon IP reputation list managed rule group (no extra subscription such as Shield Advanced).

Organization-wide audit and auto-remediation of overly permissive security group rules from one place: AWS Firewall Manager security group content audit policy with auto remediation, scoped to the organization.
AWS WAF cannot be associated with a Network Load Balancer; put an Application Load Balancer (or CloudFront) in front and associate a web ACL with AWS managed rule groups for SQL injection and XSS.

Egress domain allow-listing for instances in private subnets: AWS Network Firewall with a stateful domain list rule group (allow list), with routes from the private subnets through the firewall endpoints to the NAT gateways.
